1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif face at a comfortable size with roomy line spacing and generous padding between labels, fields and buttons, though no explicitly dyslexia-tuned typeface is evident.

2.why: No italics or all-caps are used and every passage is one or two short sentences (e.g. 'Get a six-digit identity code for this demo.'), with no dense paragraphs.

3.why: Content is laid out in a single narrow column with full-width stacked buttons and inputs that reads well at phone width, although the screenshots are rendered in a desktop viewport.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Check it is you', 'Enter your identity code' and 'Next: enter the six digits' are brief and in plain, everyday wording.

5.why: Placeholders show expected formats ('name@example.com', '123456') and the sign-in screen even shows demo credentials as worked examples.

6.why: Every step can be completed after reading a heading plus one short line; the longest text is the two-line activity-log explanation, which is not required to proceed.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard control appears anywhere, and the identity code is only visible in the browser console, forcing manual typing; the backup-code screen is never reached.

8.why: No QR code or scan/alternative-entry option is present on any of the five screens, and the authenticator enrolment step is absent.

9.why: Standard labelled email and password inputs would generally work with password managers, but no autocomplete/one-time-code attributes or password-manager affordances are observable in the screenshots.

10.why: A four-segment progress bar highlights the current stage and a large solid blue primary button dominates each screen, though the progress segments are unlabelled.

11.why: Each screen has a single clear primary action ('Sign in', 'Get identity code', 'Check code'), with only a visually subordinate outlined 'Re-request identity code' as a secondary option.

12.why: Green confirmation banners plainly state outcome and next step, e.g. 'Signed in successfully. Next: get your identity code.' and 'Your identity code was requested. Next: enter the six digits.'

13.why: The user can retry entry and there is a 'Re-request identity code' button with no lockout shown, but no reveal/hide control or recovery-code screen exists in the observed flow.

14.why: The error reads 'That code does not match. Check the six digits, or request a new code.' — it names the problem and the remedy without blaming the user.

15.why: No countdown or expiry timer appears on any screen, and step 2 explicitly states 'There is no reading timer. Take as long as you need.'
